title: Assessing Covariate-Informed Grid Load Forecasting with a Time-Series Foundation Model (abstract page)
note: arXiv abstract page, v1 submitted 6 Sep 2026, by Pendyala, Fu, Yan, Virani; presented at IJCNN 2026. Abstract: Chronos-2 on ISO New England and ENTSO-E load gains a lot from task-specific fine-tuning and is strong at short horizons, but zero-shot it trails task-specific deep learning models and its error grows faster with forecast step. No code or data link. Article licence CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

title: Assessing Covariate-Informed Grid Load Forecasting with a Time-Series Foundation Model (full text): setup
note: Setup (GE Vernova authors). Daily data, not hourly: ISO-NE daily demand for 8 zones, train 2011-2020, test 2021 (365 days), covariates dew point, dry bulb temperature, calendar; ENTSO-E daily peak for 6 countries (from fev-bench Entsoe-1H), train 2015-2018, test 2019, covariates temperature, two radiation series, calendar. Horizons 30, 60, 90 days; 30-day context; metric MAPE of the median.

title: Assessing Covariate-Informed Grid Load Forecasting with a Time-Series Foundation Model (full text): baselines
note: Baselines: small TCN, LSTM and Transformer (33k to 104k parameters) trained with the authors' own masked multi-step framework (MMMF) on the same targets and covariates, 1000 epochs. Chronos-2 is run zero-shot, LoRA fine-tuned and fully fine-tuned (20 epochs, 5 seeds, best of a 20% validation split). No naive, seasonal or regression baseline. No code or data release statement; no pre-registration.

title: Assessing Covariate-Informed Grid Load Forecasting with a Time-Series Foundation Model (full text): Table III, ISO-NE
note: Table III, ISO-NE average MAPE with covariates at H=30/60/90: zero-shot Chronos-2 6.71/10.61/15.78; LoRA 4.33/5.51/5.81; full fine-tune 4.06/5.19/5.36; best baseline (MMMF Transformer) 4.13/5.06/5.50. Without covariates: zero-shot 11.41/14.29/16.56, full fine-tune 10.07/12.10/12.87, MMMF Transformer 10.64/10.61/11.14. No intervals in the table.

title: Assessing Covariate-Informed Grid Load Forecasting with a Time-Series Foundation Model (full text): Table IV, ENTSO-E
note: Table IV, ENTSO-E average MAPE with covariates at H=30/60/90: zero-shot Chronos-2 5.63/6.57/7.67; LoRA 4.54/4.91/5.32; full fine-tune 4.31/4.66/4.86; best baseline (MMMF TCN) 4.52/4.51/4.43. Without covariates zero-shot is 5.78/6.59/7.53, so covariates barely help zero-shot here. No intervals in the table.

title: Assessing Covariate-Informed Grid Load Forecasting with a Time-Series Foundation Model (full text): horizons and limits
note: Weekly-error figure: fully fine-tuned Chronos-2 beats the MMMF models in the first weeks of the horizon, then its weekly MAPE rises and passes theirs (figure only, no numbers in the text). Calendar features help only after fine-tuning (ISO-NE H=60: 5.58 to 5.19 with cyclical encoding). The text does not say whether weather inputs are observed or forecast. Hourly week-ahead is named as future work.

title: amazon/chronos-2 model card
note: Model card: 120M-parameter encoder-only model, zero-shot, native support for past and known-future covariates, context up to 8192 and prediction length up to 1024 steps, runs on GPU or CPU, installed with chronos-forecasting 2.0 or later. Trained on subsets of Chronos Datasets and GIFT-Eval Pretrain plus synthetic data. The fetched card text shows no licence line.

title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty (abstract page)
note: Separate study (Kaljevic, Arzola, Zhang; 5 Oct 2026), abstract page fetched. Four trained-from-scratch models and four foundation models on three load datasets under different future-covariate availability. Reports Chronos-2 best both zero-shot and fine-tuned when future covariates are known or well forecast, degrading as covariate forecasts get noisy. Differs on zero-shot; not a replication.

title: Pith review page for arXiv 2609.06656 (research source 2)
note: Research call, source 2; not fetched, known from source and search snippets. A third-party automated review of the paper: says the baselines were trained for a fixed 1000 epochs without validation-based selection while Chronos-2 got checkpoint selection, that the baseline set is narrow, and that the tables give no standard deviations. Secondary commentary, not a primary source.

title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty (research source 3)
note: Research call, source 3; full text not fetched, numbers known from snippets only. Hourly day-ahead load on three public datasets including ISO-NE 2015-2019; reports ISO-NE MAE 266.25 zero-shot and 229.82 fine-tuned for Chronos-2 with covariates, against 263.98 for TimesNet. Fine-tuning helps there too; zero-shot is about level with the trained models rather than behind.

title: Explainable Load Forecasting with Covariate-Informed Time Series Foundation Models (research source 7)
note: Research call, source 7; not fetched, known from snippets. Independent study on hourly day-ahead load for a German transmission operator: zero-shot Chronos-2 with weather and calendar covariates is competitive with a Transformer trained on years of the operator's data, and covariates cut its MAE by about 27%. A different task from the candidate's; not a replication.
